title: Vana: exile
hook: Krishna comes to the forest, Draupadi tells him everything, and he explains why he wasn't there
carry: let them finish before you answer

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Vana, the forest, the sun gave Yudhishthira a vessel, and Draupadi served everyone before herself. Your line was serve someone else first. Did you pour for someone else first? Day seven hundred seventy-eight.

Chariots on a forest road. Word has reached Krishna's people that the Pandavas are in exile, and Krishna comes to find them, with kinsmen beside him. The cousins embrace. And then Draupadi speaks. She doesn't make small talk. She tells him everything: the hall, being dragged in by her hair, the laughter, the husbands who sat silent. She weeps as she speaks. And under all of it is one question she doesn't quite need to say out loud. Where were you? Today, Krishna in the forest, and his answer.
screen: `KRISHNA COMES TO THE FOREST.` → `DRAUPADI TELLS EVERYTHING.` → `WHERE WERE YOU?`

segments.voice: Notice first what Draupadi does with her grief. She doesn't tidy it. She names each wrong, in order, to the one person she trusts to hear it whole. In the epic's telling, she even says that she has no husband, no son, no friend, no brother, and not even Krishna, because none of them protected her. That is a hard thing to say to someone's face. And Krishna doesn't argue with it. He makes her a promise instead: the women of those who wronged her will one day weep as she is weeping now. Then, turning to Yudhishthira, he answers the question underneath. I wasn't there, he says. If I had been in Dvaraka, I would have come to that game uninvited and stopped it. But he was away, fighting a king named Shalva, who had attacked his city in a flying citadel. By the time he came home and heard the news, the dice had already fallen. It's a striking moment. Krishna, whom devotees worship as God, here gives an account of his absence. He doesn't say the suffering was meant to happen. He doesn't tell Draupadi to be calm. He says, in effect, I was fighting somewhere else, and had I been home, I would have stopped it. So the forest becomes a place for this kind of conversation too. Away from the palace, away from the hall, Draupadi says exactly what she thinks, even to Krishna, and Krishna stays to hear all of it before he answers.
screen: `DRAUPADI NAMES EACH WRONG.` · `KRISHNA MAKES A PROMISE.` · `I WAS FIGHTING SHALVA.` · then, large: `GRIEF SAID OUT LOUD, AND HEARD.`

segments.voice: Settle, and let the breath find its own pace. Bring to mind someone who once told you something hard: a hurt, a complaint, maybe even one that was about you. Remember how it felt to hear it. Now, with each breath out, let yourself simply listen, the way Krishna listens before he answers. No fixing, no defending. Breathe in, and make room. Breathe out, and stay. If you pray, you can bring that person into your prayer. If not, just hold them kindly in mind. The bell holds the time.
Vana. The forest of exile, where Draupadi tells Krishna everything, and Krishna says where he was.
Your line: let them finish before you answer. Today, when someone tells you something hard, let them finish before you answer. Day seven hundred seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Devotees revere Krishna as God, and storytellers dwell on this forest meeting, where Draupadi pours out her grief and Krishna promises that the wrongs done to her will be answered.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. Draupadi weeps and says that even you didn't protect her. what do you say first?
options: explain that it was all meant to be.
promise her the wrong will be answered.
tell her to be patient like Yudhishthira.
fork.reveal: he promises that the women of her tormentors will weep as she does, then explains he was away fighting Shalva.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna could have saved her and didn't bother.
what it means: he says he was away fighting Shalva, and would have stopped the game had he been in Dvaraka.
what a scholar hears: the epic lets Draupadi count even Krishna among those who failed her, and keeps the complaint on the record.
recall: warned the game would bring quarrel

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Aranyaka Parva), the arrival of Krishna in the forest (Draupadi's lament; Krishna's promise; his account of the war with Shalva and the Saubha)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Draupadi lists husbands, sons, friends, brothers and Krishna as those who failed her, and that Krishna's promise concerns the weeping of the wives of her tormentors.
Confirm Krishna's statement that he would have come uninvited to the game had he been in Dvaraka, and that he was fighting Shalva of the Saubha (flying city).

Popular tellings place Krishna's help to Draupadi in the hall (the endless garment); the script avoids contradicting that and focuses on this forest conversation. A Keeper may want a line acknowledging the hall tradition.
'Devotees worship Krishna as God' kept deliberately narrow under the claims rule.

Editor: removed 'I'm sorry I wasn't with you', an apology the epic doesn't give Krishna, in favor of his stated claim that he would have stopped the game; replaced the closing 'Vana, the forest, isn't only...' line (repeated from days 776-777) with a concrete line about Draupadi and Krishna.
Audit: in Ganguli Krishna's account of his absence (the Shalva war) is addressed to Yudhishthira, not Draupadi; teach now says he turns to Yudhishthira.
